Participant demographics (age, sex, handedness), substance use history, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. MDMA is a stimulant (substituted amphetamine), so the study falls within the meta-analysis stimulant class. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing substance-dependent individuals (poly-substance: cocaine, amphetamine, alcohol) versus healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with family-wise error cluster-level correction and provides voxel coordinates (e.g., MNI −5,53,−3) confirming voxelwise results. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (including duration of abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical human structural MRI (VBM) study of binge-drinking (alcohol) subjects vs healthy volunteers that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses. The Methods describe T1 acquisition at 3T, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), and whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons with cluster-level correction; Results report voxel-wise correlations and a between-group comparison (stated as non-significant in highlighted regions). Participant demographics, substance-use measures (AUDIT), MRI field strength, and processing software are provided. Thus it addresses the meta-analysis objective (alcohol users) and satisfies inclusion criteria for empirical GM volume comparisons with whole-brain voxel-wise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid (SC) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group SnPM VBM results (significant clusters in right frontal lobe) and also provides ROI analyses; voxelwise results and coordinates are described/mentioned. Participant demographics (male, ages reported), substance-use characteristics (SC use duration and detected compounds listed in appendix), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, SnPM) are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; study is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, limitations, appendix). Therefore include for meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs. controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM99) to compare gray matter concentration between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients (n=13) and controls (n=16). It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (corrected results, p<.01) and gives participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users vs controls that reports cortical and subcortical grey-matter measures (cortical thickness, cortical surface area, and subcortical volumes) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, MAGeTbrain). Thus it meets I2 and I5. However, analyses were restricted to a priori frontal regions-of-interest (six ROIs) and subcortical structures; the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain GM volume between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) performed at 3.0 T that reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of grey matter volumes between alcohol use disorder (AUD) participants and healthy controls, and also reports comparisons involving problem gamblers. The methods section describes MRI acquisition, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), statistical analysis (whole-brain FDR correction), and participant demographics (male-only sample, ages, AUDIT scores, abstinence duration, smoking status), satisfying reporting expectations. The paper clearly provides whole-brain voxelwise results (significant clusters reported and visualized) comparing substance users (alcohol) vs controls. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants to healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (SPM8/DARTEL). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster results, MNI/Talairach coordinates, figures, and ROC analyses (satisfying voxelwise reporting). Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI acquisition (high-resolution T1 parameters), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; it's original human MRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing brain regional volumes between substance users (alcoholics and smokers) and controls, and it reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software (FreeSurfer v5.3.0) (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses are region-of-interest/parcel-based volume comparisons using FreeSurfer parcellation rather than whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or stereotaxic coordinate tables/figures. The manuscript does not report voxelwise whole-brain GM contrasts or coordinates required by the review inclusion criterion I3. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs controls and reports total gray- and white-matter volumes and ICV, but it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts, coordinate tables, or regional voxelwise GM results (only global/volume ratios). Therefore it meets inclusion criterion I2 (empirical MRI assessing GM volume differences) but does NOT meet I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported) nor I4 (no voxelwise coordinate/figure results provided). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper provides no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (only global/region-aggregate volumes). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter density between cocaine users (a stimulant) and matched nondrug-using controls. The full text provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (tables and figures of significant clusters), reports participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of substance-related GM alterations.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine (stimulant) users to non-drug-using controls and reports cortical volume (CV) measures in addition to surface area and thickness (meets I2). The authors performed a whole-brain analysis using Freesurfer's QDEC (cluster-wise FDR q=0.05) comparing groups (meets I3). Although whole-brain results were null, a whole-brain between-group contrast was explicitly performed and reported (qualifying whole-brain evidence). The paper reports participant demographics (male, age 18–55), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software (Freesurfer v5.0), satisfying I5. Reporting of voxelwise/whole-brain results in the main text (and the null finding) makes the reporting acceptable under I4. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study (E5 not met) and it is an empirical human MRI study (E6 not met). Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical longitudinal MRI study of adolescent brain development in relation to lifetime cannabis use and psychotic-like experiences, but it does not report any whole-brain between-group GM contrast comparing substance users versus controls. Analyses focus on voxelwise regressions within an a priori hippocampus/parahippocampus mask (ROI) and mediation analyses using continuous cannabis-use measures rather than case-control GM comparisons. Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E5 met: the study reports semi-automated, observer-assisted ROI-based volumetric analyses of predefined reward regions and some global measures, but does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or VBM between-group GM contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing substance users—alcoholics—and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength and methodological details). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users but it does not include a control group nor report any whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. The analyses are correlational within a single sample and rely on ROI-based VBM/SBM measures of the right insula. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirement for between-group whole-brain GM comparisons. Exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses / no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and software) is met. Inclusion criteria I2 (between-group GM differences vs controls), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast), and I4 (whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates) are not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorder vs matched controls that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (FSL-VBM) showing significant GM density differences and confirms findings with ROI analyses. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FIRST, FAST, SIENAX), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of substance-related GM differences.

The study reports original human structural MRI data using voxel-based morphometry comparing 20 synthetic cannabinoid users to 20 healthy controls and reports between-group voxelwise gray matter differences (reduced GM in bilateral thalamus and left cerebellum). Based on the abstract and available content, it satisfies: I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM results reported), and I4 (voxelwise results are clearly reported in the text/abstract). The full text provided here is incomplete (only abstract/metadata/references present), so MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software could not be confirmed and some methodological details are missing; additionally, there is some uncertainty whether 'synthetic cannabinoids' should be grouped within the review's 'cannabis' class. Therefore inclusion is recommended but with moderate confidence and fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescent cannabis users vs controls that reports manual tracings of left and right amygdala volumes (ROI-based morphometry). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise/whole-brain GM contrast or VBM results are reported). Exclusion met: E5 (study reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks whole-brain GM comparisons required by the review (I3) and meets ROI-only exclusion (E5).

EXCLUDED because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses of manually delineated cerebellar/vermis volumes and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (ROI-only studies with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing GM volume between substance users [cannabis] and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength [1.5T], and preprocessing/statistical software details). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain voxelwise results.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing smokers (nicotine-dependent individuals) to nonsmoking controls. The paper reports voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts with FDR-corrected results and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures (Table 2, Figures 1–2). The authors also performed a whole-brain DARTEL analysis (reported in Supplementary Materials) and provide sufficient methodological detail (participant age/sex, FTND scores, scanner field strength 3.0T, preprocessing and statistical software: SPM8, SUIT, DARTEL, DPARSFA). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical report) apply. The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: E5 — this study reports only region-of-interest hippocampal analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise or VBM between-group GM contrasts. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength [1.5T], and preprocessing/statistical software [AFNI]). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 — the paper does not report any whole-brain between-group GM analyses or voxelwise results comparing substance users to controls, so it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore the study must be excluded per the review criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group ANCOVA results (SPM5) with family-wise error correction and mentions MNI coordinates converted to Talairach, and extracts regional volumes for follow-up analyses. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM) are provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI study (English) comparing alcohol-dependent subjects and controls and reports regional volumetric differences using automated subcortical and hippocampal subfield segmentation (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Analyses are ROI/subfield based (Freesurfer segmentation and ANCOVA of regional volumes), so it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses without qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with prenatal cocaine/tobacco exposure reporting regional cortical thickness and subcortical volumetric differences using Freesurfer. However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (e.g., predefined DLPFC/VMPFC thickness and specific subcortical volumes) rather than whole-brain voxelwise GM volume contrasts or coordinate tables. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only ROI-based analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM-related measures between exposed and control groups) and I5 (reports participant age, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM volume contrast reported) and I4 (no voxelwise coordinate results provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failing the whole-brain/voxelwise reporting requirement.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing daily cannabis users to nonusers with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and FreeSurfer whole-brain GLMs) of gray matter volume/density and shape. The paper reports participant demographics (age/sex counts), substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSLVBM, FreeSurfer, FIRST). Whole-brain contrasts were explicitly performed and reported (though null), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

While this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports gray-matter volume differences using FreeSurfer (I2) and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software details (I5), it does not present a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast with spatially localized results (no voxelwise coordinates, statistical maps, or whole-brain contrasts reported beyond global/ lobar and ROI summaries). The paper reports lobar and subcortical ROI-based volumes and whole-brain global measures but effectively provides only ROI/lobar analyses for localization. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI mega-analysis reporting gray matter differences between substance-dependent individuals and nondependent controls across many whole-brain FreeSurfer-defined regions (82 ROIs). The full text includes introduction, methods (T1 acquisition, FreeSurfer v5.3 preprocessing, statistical modeling), results (whole-brain ROI comparisons, cross-validation), and discussion. Participant age/sex and substance characteristics and scanner/acquisition details are reported (main text and supplement). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM volume comparisons (I2), reports whole-brain between-group contrasts across the brain via comprehensive ROI analyses (I3), and provides key participant and methods details (I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-limited without whole-brain results, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent subjects (including subgroups: ‘pure’ alcoholics and polysubstance-abusing alcoholics) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with permutation-based nonparametric testing and displays/describes significant voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM v1.1, BET, FAST, FLIRT, FNIRT) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study reporting regional cortical morphometry in substance-using groups vs. controls (meets I2). It reports participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/software (FreeSurfer v5.1) (meets I5). However, the study presents ROI-based FreeSurfer parcellation results (ACC, DPFC, OFC, insula) and univariate ROI analyses rather than any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Therefore it does not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM contrasts (I3) and falls under exclusion E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing treatment-seeking cocaine users (iCUD) with healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (Group main effects and planned whole-brain comparisons) with coordinate tables/figures (Table 2, Figure 1), satisfying voxelwise reporting. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM volume studies of a substance user group (stimulants) vs controls. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder (stimulant users) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (including cluster coordinates, sizes and corrected p-values) and a between-group contrast (controls > CUD) for the mid-cingulate cortex, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, and it is empirical human MRI work). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusions.

Full text appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study examines adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (not current substance users), so it does not meet inclusion criterion I2 (between substance users and controls). The abstract indicates surface-based whole-brain maps of gray matter asymmetry (I3 met), and mentions traditional volumetric ROI analyses; however, without the full text I cannot verify voxelwise whole-brain GM volume contrasts or full methodological details. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are explicitly met (E5 and E6 not applicable). Therefore, exclude due to failure to meet I2 and incomplete full text preventing confirmation of other required details.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volumes between heavy alcohol-using adolescents/young adults and matched light-drinking controls. The paper reports a whole-brain VBM between-group contrast (stating no significant clusters on whole-brain analysis) and ROI-corrected voxelwise results with coordinates/figures for regions showing reduced GM in users. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (AUDIT-C history), MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volume between binge-drinking (alcohol-using) young adults and matched healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (cluster extent threshold and voxelwise results) and also reports SVC results; voxel coordinates, statistical thresholds, preprocessing (SPM8/DARTEL), scanner field strength (3T), and participant demographics are provided. The study directly addresses alcohol (one of the meta-analysis drug classes) and provides qualifying whole-brain GM differences suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=24) and healthy controls (n=24) using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for grey matter volume and reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts. The paper provides voxelwise results (coordinates and figures), details participant age/sex, alcohol use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for grey matter volume whole-brain analyses in a substance-using (alcohol) sample. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not incomplete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study of alcohol users (I2 met). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses relating AUDIT scores to GMV and provides coordinate information and preprocessing/MRI details (I4 and I5 met). However, the study does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users versus non-user controls (no categorical GMV case-control contrast); rather, it uses dimensional regression across a continuum of drinking severity. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (required: at least one whole-brain between-group substance users vs controls contrast). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing prenatal cocaine-exposed children to non-exposed controls and reports regional gray matter volumes and participant/MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses are region-based (automated FreeSurfer volumetry of cortical and subcortical structures) and do not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or spatial coordinates suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence criterion (I3) and effectively falls under exclusion E5 (ROI/volume-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical longitudinal MRI study in nonhuman primates (rhesus macaques) of voluntary ethanol self-administration showing within-subject cortical volume change. It does not provide a between-group comparison of substance users versus controls in humans (no separate control group of non-users; analyses are within-subject and across drinking levels in monkeys). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls) or I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). It does meet I5 (reports age/sex, MRI field strength, and processing details). No exclusion criteria (E5 or E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing active heavy drinkers (substance users) with age- and sex-matched light-drinking controls using volumetric measures of gray matter. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise deformation morphometry (ANCOVA and regression maps) comparing HD vs LD, with permutation and cluster-based correction procedures and illustrated t-statistical maps, satisfying whole-brain between-group contrasts. It also provides participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and detailed preprocessing/segmentation and statistical methods. The study is not ROI-only and is not a review. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

EXCLUDED because the study reports segmented regional volumes across seven axial slices and lateral/third ventricular volumes rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group grey-matter contrast. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI/partial-slice analyses only, no qualifying whole-brain results). The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses on frontal and temporal lobe slabs (manual tracings over a seven-slice contiguous volume) with no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, and MRI field strength). This study is an empirical 3T structural MRI investigation of nicotine-dependent smokers vs nonsmokers and reports GM volume analyses focused on insular subregions (anterior/posterior insula) and seed-based structural covariance. It does not present a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of GM volume with reported coordinates or cluster results comparing substance users vs controls. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between users and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study comparing subjects with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to matched controls. It reports whole-brain analyses of gray matter (volumetric and surface-based cortical thickness) using FreeSurfer/Qdec with appropriate multiple-comparison correction and presents between-group voxelwise/surface-wise results. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (age, sex, smoking status, current alcohol consumption, duration) and MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons in substance users (alcohol) and has no exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescent smokers to nonsmoker controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reporting significant GMV differences (vmPFC) with cluster coordinates and statistics. The paper reports participant age (14-year-olds), demographic info, smoking exposure measures, MRI field strength (3T across sites), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 for VBM; FSL for DTI). Whole-brain GM analyses and coordinate/cluster results are clearly presented; voxelwise results are reported with coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds. The study addresses nicotine use and meets the review objective. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing gray matter measures between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls (meets I2). The paper reports hippocampal GM volume estimates (Hipp/TIV ratio and anterodorsal hippocampal ROI volumes) derived from voxel-based morphometry and uses SPM8 (meets I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts or provide whole-brain coordinate tables/figures for GM differences between substance users and controls. The analyses and results are focused on hippocampal/ROI measures rather than qualifying whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent (ADO and PS) groups to healthy controls and reports GM-related measurements (global GM/CSF) and regional subcortical volumes obtained via model-based segmentation. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/analysis tools). However, the study reports ROI-based volumetric analyses of segmented subcortical structures and global GM/CSF, not a voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrast (no VBM or other whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates reported). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). I3 (requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to age- and gender-matched non-smokers with whole-brain between-group contrasts reported (cluster- and voxel-level results, tables/figures with MNI coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use measures (years smoked, cigarettes/day, FTND, pack-years), MRI field strength (3T Siemens TIM Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (DARTEL, SPM8, MATLAB) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the nicotine (tobacco) class and should be included.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports cerebellar grey- and white-matter volumes using manual parcellation and provides participant demographics and MRI details (I2 and I5 are satisfied). However, the paper does not report a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrast of grey matter volume; analyses are limited to cerebellar parcellation/ROI-based volumes (no qualifying whole-brain GM contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for the cerebellar-focused study (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that directly compares adolescents with alcohol use disorder (substance users) to matched healthy controls. The manuscript reports voxelwise group analyses (AUD vs HC) using VBM in SPM8 and provides MNI coordinates for reported clusters (even if findings are uncorrected), satisfying the requirement that between-group voxelwise GM contrasts are available. MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM), and participant demographics/substance-use measures are described. Although ROI masks from the AAL atlas were used based on prior hypotheses, the paper still reports voxelwise results with coordinates and whole-brain VBM procedures and multiple-comparison correction procedures are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study that reports whole-brain vertexwise analyses (cortical thickness and volumetric measures) comparing children prenatally exposed to cannabis/tobacco vs nonexposed controls. It satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (reports whole-brain between-group GM contrast using vertexwise analyses), I4 (voxelwise/vertexwise results reported in the main text with clusterwise statistics), and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I2 because the comparison is between offspring with prenatal exposure and controls, not between substance-using participants and controls; the meta-analysis objective specifically targets studies of substance users (current/former users) vs controls. No exclusion criteria (e.g., E5 ROI-only or E6 non-empirical) are met. The full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing early-onset chronic cannabis users to matched controls (meets I2). The paper reports whole-brain between-group analyses (two-sample t-tests) and explicitly states a whole-brain finding: increased left postcentral gyrus gray matter in cannabis users (meets I3). Voxelwise results and ROI-masked analyses are reported with coordinates and statistical thresholds (meets I4). Participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM toolbox, DARTEL) are described (meets I5). No exclusion criteria are met: the study includes whole-brain voxelwise results (E5 not applicable) and is empirical human MRI research (E6 not applicable). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports only region-of-interest analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I2 (does not report GM volume differences between substance users and controls — sample includes only MJ users, no control group), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast reported), I4 (no voxelwise whole-brain coordinate results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these, the paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirements and should be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter and white matter tissue density between heavy cannabis users (n=11) and non-using controls (n=8). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (with cluster-level correction) and provides MNI coordinates for significant GM clusters (including hippocampal small-volume results). MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM99 and VBM procedures), participant sex and substance-use characteristics are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small and all participants are male, the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume/density comparisons and reports coordinate-based voxelwise results, so it is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract this is an empirical 1.5T MRI study reporting gray matter volume deficits in alcoholic patients vs controls, so I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison) is met. However, I cannot confirm whether at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (I3) is reported, nor whether coordinate tables/figures for voxelwise results are available (I4). Reporting of participant details and preprocessing/software is incomplete in the abstract (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are clearly met. Because the full text is not available to verify whole-brain results and requisite detail, I must exclude this study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical longitudinal structural MRI study of alcohol exposure in college students, but it does not report a whole‑brain between-group comparison of substance users vs. controls. Instead, the authors report voxelwise associations within a hippocampus/parahippocampus mask (ROI-based longitudinal associations with a continuous alcohol-use index). Therefore it violates E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). It does satisfy I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI acquisition details, preprocessing and software). It does NOT satisfy I2 (no case-control GM volume comparison of substance users vs controls) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Exclusion ID met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I2, I3 (also I4 not applicable because voxelwise results are within an ROI mask rather than whole-brain between-group results).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter volumes between methamphetamine-dependent users (n=34) and non-user controls (n=31). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. MRI acquisition (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL for segmentation; SAS for stats) are reported, and participant demographics, age/sex, and substance-use characteristics are detailed. The study performed whole-brain regional analyses by segmenting the entire cortex into six main lobes and 17 subregions (whole-brain coverage) and conducted between-group contrasts (ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANCOVA) comparing GM volumes between users and controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Coordinate tables/voxelwise maps are not necessary per I4 since whole-brain ROI-based contrasts are reported in the main text/tables. The study pertains to a stimulant (methamphetamine), matching the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI VBM study of cocaine use disorder comparing users and controls (I2 satisfied). However, the manuscript does NOT report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls; group comparisons were conducted using predefined bilateral rACC ROIs and ROI-based VBM, and the authors explicitly state they did not perform whole-brain group difference analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of adolescent cannabis users vs. controls that reports PFC volumetric differences derived from manual ROI tracing and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical tools—thus satisfying I2 and I5. However, the paper reports only region-of-interest analyses (manual PFC ROIs) and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts, coordinate tables, or voxelwise maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E5 (no whole-brain GM comparisons).

This study was excluded because it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/volume-based GM comparisons. Although it is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study and reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer) (I5 met), the paper reports cortical thickness (surface-based) measures and regional/parcellation ROI analyses (frontal regions) rather than gray matter volume/density voxelwise contrasts. No whole-brain VBM-style between-group GM volume results with coordinates are reported; the authors note a whole-brain check for interactions but present ROI-based parcellation results and no qualifying voxelwise/coordinate tables (I2 not met, I3 not met, I4 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion applied: E5. Inclusion met: I5. Inclusion not met: I2, I3, I4.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM5/VBM5.1) comparing gray matter between cocaine users (stimulant class) and demographically matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group analyses (ANCOVA and voxel-wise regression) with corrected results (cluster-level FWE and small-volume corrections) showing reduced GM in CUD versus controls (left VLPFC and OFC) and provides coordinates and statistical thresholds. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (4-T), preprocessing, and software are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; is empirical primary data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of nicotine users that reports GM volume differences (right caudate) using automated subcortical segmentation (FreeSurfer) and provides participant demographics and method details. However, the structural analyses are limited to ROI/subcortical volume comparisons (segmented caudate, putamen, NAc) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (e.g., VBM or whole-brain surface-based analysis). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper is an empirical, whole-brain MRI study using tensor-based morphometry comparing children with prenatal methamphetamine and/or alcohol exposure to unexposed controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise contrasts, participant ages/sex, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics. However, it does not compare substance users versus controls (participants are prenatally exposed children, not active or former substance users), so it fails inclusion criterion I2. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected VBM results) and regional ROI analyses, with coordinate/cluster results and figures described. Participant sample characteristics (N by sex, drinking history, abstinence/relapse status), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8; modulation, smoothing, covariates) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study of smokers vs never-smokers and reports voxelwise cerebellar coordinates and methodological details, but the analysis is restricted to the cerebellum/brainstem using the SUIT toolbox (i.e., a region-focused, infratentorial mask) rather than a whole-brain GM volume contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only region-of-interest/infratentorial analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I4 (voxelwise result reported as coordinates/figures), I5 (participant and MRI/preprocessing/statistical details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude under E5.

This study is an empirical MRI study of chronic alcoholics vs controls and reports hippocampal and temporal lobe volumetry, but the available full text appears limited to abstract/metadata. Crucially, the paper reports region-of-interest volumetric analyses (anterior vs posterior hippocampus, temporal lobe measures) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrasts required by the review. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only, no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex and some substance-use characteristics). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported) and I4 (no voxelwise/coordinate whole-brain results available in the provided content). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent participants and healthy controls using whole-brain lobar and subcortical segmentation and between-group contrasts at multiple time points. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition at 1.5T, segmentation/preprocessing details), Results (cross-sectional comparisons vs. controls and longitudinal analyses), and Discussion. It reports whole-brain regional (lobar and subcortical) GM volume differences between substance users (alcohol) and controls rather than being limited to a single small ROI, and provides participant demographics and MRI details. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical sMRI GM volume comparisons and whole-brain between-group contrasts; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical MRI study (satisfies I2) comparing alcohol-dependent individuals and light-drinking controls. However, the analyses are based on automated segmentation into lobes and subcortical structures (lobar/ROI volumetry) rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or statistical maps. No qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results are reported in the provided full text, so the study does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray-matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls (whole-brain 2-sample t-tests reported). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts and voxelwise regression results (figures, peak coordinates, and supplemental Table S1), and provides participant demographics (age/sex), substance-use details, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5/SPM5). All inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) that reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses of gray matter density changes between smokers and never-smoker controls. Methods include acquisition of T1-weighted images (1.5T), preprocessing and tensor-based morphometry with SPM5, and between-group contrasts (UQ vs NS, SQ vs NS) reported in text and Supplementary Table S2. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength, and analysis software are reported. The study is not ROI-only and contains original voxelwise whole-brain results suitable for coordinate extraction. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (CUD vs CON) with voxelwise results presented in tables and figures, specifies MRI field strength (4 Tesla), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1), and provides participant demographics (male, ages) and detailed substance-use characteristics (years of cocaine, alcohol, smoking). The study is not ROI-only and contains original data. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing grey matter volume between heavy cannabis users (n=33) and matched controls (n=42). The paper reports voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts (whole-brain analysis with a priori ROI masks and thresholds for whole-brain findings) and within-group voxelwise regressions relating GM volume to cannabis use measures. Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that compares gray matter (and white matter) volumes between nicotine-dependent smokers and age-matched non-smoker controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (smokers vs. controls and subgroups) with corrected thresholds and presents region-level results (figures and tables). Participant demographics, substance-use measures (pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL, DPABI) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study investigating gray matter volume differences between infants with prenatal alcohol exposure and matched controls (substance class: alcohol). MRI was done on a 3T scanner and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, SPM8) and participant demographics (age, sex, ethnicity) and substance-use characteristics (ASSIST, exposure timing/quantity) are reported. The analysis used whole-brain atlas-based volumetry (90 AAL regions) with between-group contrasts and multiple-region regressions; results are presented in tables/figures and supplementary materials (satisfying whole-brain reporting). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Although the exposed cohort are neonates with in utero exposure rather than active adult users, the study directly assesses structural GM differences due to alcohol exposure and thus meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for the alcohol class.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter (GMD) between heroin-dependent (opioid) users and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANOVA on modulated gray matter segments) and provides coordinate/region-level results (frontal, cingulate, occipital reductions). Key methodological details are reported: participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (GE Signa 1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, VBM). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Study is directly relevant to the opioid class in the meta-analysis and meets inclusion criteria I2–I5.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs controls and reports regional GM volume differences (insula, amygdala) and participant/MRI details, but it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (e.g., VBM or other whole-brain statistical maps). Analyses are manual ROI morphometry of the insula and automated subcortical segmentation (FIRST) for the amygdala and supplementary region volumes; no whole-brain results or coordinate-based voxelwise findings are presented. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison) and I5 (participant/MRI/method details reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast) and I4 (no voxelwise/coordinate results provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical English MRI study reporting grey-matter-related measures (cortical volume and thickness) between substance-dependent individuals and controls (I2 satisfied) and provides whole-brain vertex-wise thickness maps/figures (I4) and participant/substance/MR acquisition and preprocessing details (I5), it does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume/density/concentration (voxelwise or surface-based volume maps) that the review requires. The paper’s whole-brain analyses were vertex-wise tests of cortical thickness (not whole-brain GM volume contrasts), and cortical volume comparisons were reported only as region-of-interest results. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain GM volume evidence) is not met. Because no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results are provided, exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only studies with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (VBM) comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=20) and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume comparisons (SPM8/DARTEL VBM) with FWE-corrected results and provides coordinates/figures of significant GMV reductions. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (severity, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain results), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (participant/MRI/method details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing 22 alcohol-dependent patients to 22 matched healthy controls with whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. The paper reports whole-brain GM and WM differences (tables/figures), provides participant age/sex and substance-use details (duration and daily consumption), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (optimised VBM protocol, SPM2). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only analysis, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing young adult recreational cannabis users (n=20) to matched controls (n=20) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density), regional volume, and shape analyses. The paper reports whole-brain VBM contrasts with voxelwise cluster results (Tables/Figures) and provides participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FreeSurfer). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I2,I3,I4,I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears to include Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients and controls and reports volumetric differences (subcortical volumes and total gray/white matter) using FSL segmentation and vertex analysis (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts (e.g., VBM or whole-brain Randomise voxelwise GM maps). Analyses are ROI-based (FIRST segmentation and vertex/surface analyses of subcortical structures) and global total gray-matter volume comparisons, so it lacks qualifying whole-brain GM results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/region-based results without whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion met: I2, I5. Inclusion not met: I3 (whole-brain voxelwise GM contrast). Exclusion met: E5.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volume between binge-drinking alcohol users and matched controls. The paper reports both ROI and an exploratory whole-brain between-group analysis (whole-brain results reported at P<0.001 uncorrected with coordinates/clusters), and provides coordinate tables/figures and correlation analyses. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for alcohol studies with voxelwise whole-brain GM contrasts and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM-DARTEL) study comparing gray matter volume/concentration between chronic cannabis users (n=11) and matched controls (n=13). The paper reports whole-brain VBM analyses (unmodulated and modulated data) and a between-group contrast showing reduced right anterior hippocampal GM volume in users (MNI coordinates reported) and regression analyses correlating THC/CBD with hippocampal GM; voxelwise results and coordinates are provided. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. Although the hippocampal volume finding did not survive FWE correction after small-volume correction and sample size is small, the study nevertheless meets inclusion requirements for whole-brain voxelwise GM comparisons between substance users and controls and supplies coordinate-based results for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (combined voxel-wise P<0.001 and cluster-extent thresholds with PFWE<0.05), provides MNI coordinates and cluster sizes in results/tables and figures, and describes participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (VBM8, SPM8). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing 30 codeine-containing cough syrup (CCS) users to 30 matched controls and reporting significant between-group GM volume reductions (vmPFC) with stereotactic coordinates and corrected statistics. Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/software (VBM8, SPM8), participant details and impulsivity measures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain voxelwise GM comparisons in an opioid-using group relevant to the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users and matched healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise VBM analyses (whole-brain processing described) and presents between-group contrasts with coordinates (referenced Tables/Figures) showing reduced VMPFC gray matter in CUD (ROI-corrected FWE) and notes whole-brain results (no other clusters survived whole-brain correction). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without whole-brain analyses; not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text presents an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs healthy controls using automated hippocampal subfield segmentation (FreeSurfer) and reports subfield volumes (CA2+3, CA4+DG, subiculum) and longitudinal changes. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study comparing GM volume between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criterion I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast) is NOT met: the study focuses on hippocampal subfield ROI segmentation and statistical comparisons of those regions; no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast is reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Decision: EXCLUDED due to E5. Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3. Exclusion IDs met: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing nicotine-dependent smokers (n=80) to matched non-smoking controls (n=80). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E5, E6).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume/density between smokers and never-smokers. (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of substance users vs controls is reported — analyses use global GM ratio and gene-association regressions rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts or coordinate results), I4 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures/supplementary whole-brain results are provided or indicated).
