This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study of alcohol consumption in a community sample, but it does not present a between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. The analysis is a voxelwise regression associating amount of alcohol consumption with regional GM/WM volumes across participants rather than comparing a discrete group of alcohol users to a control group. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I2 (study must assess GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). It does satisfy permissive reporting criteria (I4: voxelwise results reported) and demographic/method details (I5). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent subjects (a stimulant class) to non-drug-using controls using voxel-wise methods (TBM and VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group analyses conducted with SPM8 (voxel-wise FWE correction across the whole brain) and presents the null results; therefore whole-brain contrasts of GM volume were performed and are available. Participant demographics, age/gender, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This study used voxel-based morphometry confined to 13 a priori small-volume templates (small volume correction / masked ROIs) rather than reporting at least one whole-brain between-group (substance users vs controls) voxelwise contrast. Exclusion ID met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM density differences between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported with cluster coordinates/statistics), I5 (reports participant/substance-use details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI/VBM study comparing long-term abstinent alcoholics to controls (meets I2). The authors report both ROI-restricted VBM results (significant amygdala findings) and explicitly state that whole-brain (non-ROI) analyses were performed (and yielded no significant voxels), satisfying the requirement for a reported whole-brain between-group contrast (I3). Voxelwise results are presented in figures and described in the text (I4). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, FSL BET) are reported (I5). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences between substance users (alcohol) and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study comparing male methamphetamine users to healthy controls and includes whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (HC vs MA baseline) and detailed voxelwise coordinate results and repeated-measures whole-brain analyses. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing (VBM8, DARTEL) and software (SPM8) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

Although this is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of smokers and nonsmokers using whole-brain VBM (N=81 smokers, 42 nonsmokers) and reports voxelwise GMV results (interaction cluster in left medial OFC with coordinates), it does NOT present a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users (nicotine smokers) versus controls comparing GM volume. The main reported VBM result is a genotype × smoking interaction rather than a direct smoker vs. nonsmoker GMV contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume; includes smokers and controls), I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (E5 and E6 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcoholic patients and matched control subjects with quantitative measures of cortical gray matter and CSF volumes over time. The methods describe whole-brain segmentation across seven axial slices sampling approximately half the brain and report global cortical gray matter and regional cortical volumes and group-by-time contrasts between alcohol users and controls. Participant age ranges, drinking behavior, scanner field strength (1.5 T), and image-processing/statistical approaches are reported. The paper therefore provides whole-brain (global and regionally parcellated) GM volume comparisons between substance users (alcohol) and controls and meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between occasional amphetamine-type stimulant/cocaine users (N=165) and stimulant-naïve controls (N=48). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses (linear mixed effects model) and whole-brain regressions relating lifetime use to regional GM volume, with coordinates and cluster results described. Methods report participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FNIRT, FLIRT, AFNI, R). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, between-group structural MRI comparison of substance users versus controls. Instead it reports manual ROI (lingula/lobule I) measurements and correlational analyses of alcohol/drug use within a community sample stratified by maltreatment history; substance dependence cases were excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports participant age/sex and MRI field strength and other methodological details). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not present an empirical GM volume case-control comparison of substance users vs controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain GM differences between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of 39 heavy drinking smokers, but it does not include a control group or any between-group contrasts of substance users vs. controls. Inclusion criteria I2 (studies assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (reporting at least one whole-brain between-group contrast users vs controls) are not met. The study does satisfy I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting required between-group whole-brain comparison criteria.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistics software (VBM8/SPM8) (meets I5). However, it does not report a qualifying whole‑brain voxelwise between‑group contrast or provide coordinates/voxelwise regional results: results present only a global whole‑brain gray matter volume difference and discussion of metabolites; no voxelwise statistical maps, cluster tables, or coordinates are provided in the main text or supplements. Therefore it does not meet I3 (whole‑brain between‑group contrast) nor I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI‑only analyses or non‑empirical paper) explicitly apply beyond failure to meet inclusion criteria. Because the meta‑analysis objective is to identify consistent regional GM alterations (requires voxelwise whole‑brain results/coordinates), this study must be excluded.

Full text is complete. This is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain between-group contrasts and adequate reporting of demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing (SPM12). However, the primary between-group comparisons are former regular users (FRUs) versus former light users (FLUs) rather than substance users versus non-user healthy controls. The meta-analysis requires studies comparing substance users to controls; here the ‘control’ group consists of light/former users and subjects who never used substances were excluded from analyses. Therefore inclusion criterion I2 is not met, so the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of cocaine-dependent individuals vs controls (meets I2). The report provides voxelwise OFC results and figures (meets I4) and reports participant characteristics and preprocessing/software (meets I5). However, the analyses were constrained to an a priori orbitofrontal cortex region and the paper focuses on OFC voxelwise/regressions and OFC volume comparisons; no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast of substance users vs controls is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion: E5. Included criteria met: I2, I4, I5. Inclusion criterion not met: I3.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter between alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (GM density reductions in AUDs vs. controls) with tables/figures of voxelwise results and conjunction/interaction analyses. Methods report participant age/sex, alcohol use variables, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, DARTEL). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This study reports structural MRI in 60 alcohol-dependent subjects with FreeSurfer segmentation and relates gray-matter volumes to executive performance, but it does not include a control group or any between-group (substance users vs. controls) whole-brain contrast. Therefore it does not meet the review's requirement for between-group GM comparisons. Exclusion rationale: No qualifying whole-brain between-group results reported. Inclusion/exclusion summary provided below.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing whole-brain gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients and matched controls. The Methods report a whole-brain between-groups VBM analysis with results (greater GM volume in right caudate and right orbitofrontal gyri) presented in figures/tables. MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical approaches are described (with supporting information). The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group VBM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (participant demographics, substance-use details, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistics provided). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI VBM study of alcohol binge drinkers vs controls and reports voxelwise GM density differences, but the analysis is ROI-restricted (masking the prefrontal–striatal inhibitory circuitry) rather than an unbiased whole-brain between-group contrast. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM density/volume differences), I4 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables), and I5 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Hence the study is excluded under E5.

This is an empirical human MRI study that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing gray matter volume between cocaine use disorder (CUD) participants and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain 2 (Diagnosis) × 2 (PENK) ANCOVA VBM results with cluster-corrected thresholds and identifies a significant Diagnosis × PENK interaction in right inferior frontal gyrus gray matter volume, indicating whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM differences. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8), and substance-use/sample characteristics and demographic covariates are described in the methods. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM group comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), and I5 (reporting of key methodological/participant details) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study assessing gray matter morphometry in alcohol-dependent individuals vs controls (meets I2). The paper reports participant demographics and methodological details (meets I5). However, the analysis is ROI-based (Destrieux atlas regions: anterior/posterior insula and ACC) and statistical comparisons are reported for these predefined ROIs using MANCOVA and post-hoc tests. No whole-brain voxel-wise GM volume/density/concentration between-group contrasts, nor stereotactic coordinate tables or voxelwise results, are reported in the main text or supplements. Therefore it does not meet the required whole-brain evidence criterion (I3) and falls under exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI investigation using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between lifetime heroin-dependent individuals and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts demonstrating decreased gray matter density in multiple regions (prefrontal, anterior cingulate, temporal, insula, cerebellum) and presents correlation analyses with duration of heroin use. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (duration, abstinence, nicotine/alcohol info), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2, SPM2, MATLAB) are described. This is not an ROI-only study or a non-empirical paper. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and age-/gender-matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (One-Way ANCOVA and post-hoc comparisons) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinate/results in supplemental tables. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (CAT12) and statistical software (SPM12), and participant demographics (age/sex) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the alcohol substance class and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports a whole-brain FWE-corrected between-group contrast identifying reduced GMV in the left inferior frontal gyrus with MNI coordinates and Z/p-values, and extracts mean GMV for correlations with stop-signal task performance. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use measures (LTDH, AUDIT), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are reported. Thus it directly addresses the review objective (alcohol users vs controls) and satisfies all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) with no exclusion criteria met.

Full text is not available in the provided content (only title, journal metadata, and purchase/access notice). I cannot verify core methods or results. The study appears to examine individuals with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (exposure in utero) rather than current substance users, so it likely does not meet the review population requirement (studies comparing substance users vs controls). I cannot confirm whether whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts are reported. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete full text preventing assessment of I2 and I3. If full text were available, the in utero exposure population would still likely not meet the meta-analysis focus on substance users, but that cannot be confirmed here.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing cannabis users vs non-users. The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (SPM8) with region-level results (including family-wise error correction) and follow-up voxelwise/ROI analyses. Participant characteristics (mean age, familial risk, sex used as covariate), substance use measures (lifetime cannabis, alcohol, cigarettes), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL, SPSS) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=95) to healthy controls (n=87) using voxel-based morphometry. The authors report whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (2-sample t-test, FWE-corrected) with reported coordinates and clusters, and also present ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly available. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol dependence, days abstinent), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing long-term abstinent alcoholics (LTAA) to non-alcoholic controls, reporting regional gray matter volume differences using an atlas-based ROI approach across lobes and Brodmann areas. It meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). However, the study reports only ROI-based analyses (lobar/Brodmann-area aggregates) and does not present a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or voxelwise coordinate tables/figures that would qualify as whole-brain evidence. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED for failing I3 and meeting E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing non-treatment-seeking cocaine-dependent (stimulant) males to non-drug controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (with coordinates and figures) showing reduced GM in left middle frontal gyrus and reports voxel-wise correlations (coordinates) with impulsivity. Methods report participant age range/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8). This is not an ROI-only or non-empirical paper and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of crack-cocaine (stimulant) users vs controls that reports GM volume differences and provides participant/MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses extract regional cortical volumes using predefined ROIs (prefrontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or coordinate-based voxelwise results. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain results (fails I3) and constitutes an ROI-only analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Conclusion: EXCLUDED (E5).

This is an empirical structural MRI study (VBM) comparing cannabis users and controls and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the VBM analysis was restricted to the (para)hippocampal region using a small-volume/ROI approach and no whole-brain between-group voxelwise gray-matter contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and provides ROI-only structural results, which triggers exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Thus the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain GM alterations.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cannabis users versus non-users and reporting voxelwise longitudinal GM differences (tensor-based morphometry). The paper implemented a whole-brain between-group contrast (GM loss in cannabis consumers vs non-consumers) and supplemented it with small-volume corrections; coordinates and statistical results for significant voxelwise findings (after SVC) are reported. Participant demographics (age, sex) and MRI parameters (1-T scanner) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/SPM5 TBM pipeline) are described. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, original empirical data). Full text appears complete.

This empirical VBM study of cocaine-dependent (stimulant) vs controls meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical English-language MRI study reporting GM volume differences), I4 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables for ROIs), and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing and SPM2). However, the VBM analysis was restricted to a predefined set of nine ROIs using WFU PickAtlas templates rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast. Therefore it constitutes an ROI-only analysis with no qualifying whole-brain results and must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol-using (binge drinking) participants vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details (meets I5). However, the study uses manual ROI-only segmentation of the nucleus accumbens and caudate (no whole-brain or voxelwise between-group GM contrasts are reported), so it violates E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (whole-brain evidence) and I4 (voxelwise/coordinate whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure vs non-exposed controls that reports ACC volume/area/thickness from Freesurfer parcellation (ROI analyses). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM structural measures between exposed and control groups) and I5 (participant age/sex and MRI details reported). However it does NOT meet I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported); results focus on ACC ROIs only. Therefore E5 applies (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing prenatal alcohol-exposed adults to nonexposed controls using voxel-based morphometry and ROI volumetrics. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise GM/WM comparisons (VBM) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and presents voxelwise results in figures and described analyses. Participant/sample details, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SPM2) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for GM volume comparison (I2), whole-brain voxelwise evidence (I3), acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I4), and reports necessary participant/MRI/preprocessing details (I5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not a review). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Although it is an empirical, whole-brain voxelwise MRI study of brain changes in alcohol use (reports voxelwise results and figures), it analyzes longitudinal within-subject deformation tensor morphometry in a sample of alcohol-dependent subjects comparing abstainers vs relapsers rather than comparing substance users to healthy controls. It therefore does not assess grey matter volume differences between substance users and controls (I2 not met) and does not report a whole‑brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls (I3 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (acceptable reporting of voxelwise whole‑brain results in figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I2, I3 (also I5: sex information not clearly reported, though some participant and MRI details are present). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder (substance class: alcohol) to healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA and regression) with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results (e.g., superior temporal gyrus) and provides participant demographics, substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Voxelwise results are reported in tables/coordinates and described in text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only or non-empirical).

The study is excluded because it reports ROI-based analyses limited to 24 preselected ‘cue reactivity’ regions rather than providing a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language human MRI study assessing GM volume differences between heavy drinkers and light-drinker controls) and I5 (reports participant ages/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/VBM8/DARTEL)). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain evidence, this paper does not qualify despite relevant findings on alcohol-related GM differences in adolescents, particularly because the analyses are constrained to ROIs only.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine-exposed monkeys (N=7) to saline controls (N=7) with voxel-wise morphometry and behavioral/PET correlations. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance-exposed vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), I5 (participant age/sex, dosing, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (does NOT report a whole-brain between-group contrast corrected across the entire brain; analyses were confined to a predefined set of ROIs and corrected for the search volume within those ROIs rather than whole-brain inference). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (analyses are effectively ROI-restricted with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, the study uses non-human (vervet monkey) subjects which makes it incompatible with the human-focused meta-analysis scope, reinforcing exclusion. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

While this is an empirical English-language VBM study of methamphetamine users and controls that reports whole-brain voxelwise results relating D2/D3 BP and craving to gray-matter volume, the full text does not present a direct whole-brain between-group contrast (substance users vs. controls) of GM volume. The analyses focus on group-by-receptor interactions and within-group correlations rather than a main effect GM comparison between users and controls. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), although it satisfies I2, I4 and I5. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I2: it reports cortical thickness using surface-based morphometry rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration measures required by the review. It does meet I3 (reports whole-brain vertex-wise between-group contrasts corrected for multiple comparisons), I4 (whole-brain voxel/vertex-wise results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material), and I5 (reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met. Full text is complete and sufficient for this determination.

This study reports only ROI-based subcortical volumetric analyses (seven predefined subcortical ROIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text is available and complete for assessment.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM) comparing grey matter between alcohol users and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM) with cluster-corrected results and provides coordinate-based correlational analyses. Key study details are reported: participant demographics (age range, all male), substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol abuse, years and amount of use), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5, detailed pipeline). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing heavy cannabis users (n=20 persistent CB) to matched healthy controls (n=22) with voxelwise VBM analyses. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates, e.g., superior temporal gyrus and medial temporal clusters) and ROI analyses, with voxelwise results presented and described. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM VBM8, DARTEL), and substance use measures (CUDIT, grams/week). Full introduction, methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants and controls (meets I2). The paper reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical methods (3T scanner, ANTs/FSL/FreeSurfer, etc.), satisfying I5. However, the analyses are atlas/parcellation-based regional (lobar and frontal subregions) ROI volume comparisons rather than voxel-wise whole-brain between-group contrasts with coordinate-based results. The study does not present qualifying whole‑brain voxelwise contrasts/tables of coordinates required by I3. Therefore it is excluded under E5 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between stimulant-dependent patients and matched healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (two-way ANCOVA, FWE cluster-corrected) with figures and coordinates, as well as ROI cross-validation. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and is original human MRI data. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (VBM) comparing heavy smokers (n=16) to matched non-smoker controls and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates. The paper provides between-group GM contrasts (VBM) and reports MNI coordinates for GM reductions in bilateral cerebellar tonsil (with small-volume correction) and describes whole-brain thresholding procedures; demographic, substance-use (cigarettes/day, years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, PROBID for SVM) are reported. Voxelwise results are given in-text with coordinates and figures. Although some GM results are reported with small-volume correction, the study conducted whole-brain VBM and provides qualifying voxelwise results; therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E5/E6).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter density between 63 opiate-dependent subjects and 46 matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (VBM) with corrected statistical thresholds and presents regional results in text/tables and figures (prefrontal, insular, temporal GM decreases). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (including methadone treatment and comorbid substance history), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99, VBM procedures) are described. The study is not an ROI-only analysis nor a non-empirical paper. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical English-language VBM study of heroin-dependent men providing voxelwise coordinates and full methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI VBM study), I4 (voxelwise coordinates reported), I5 (participant age/sex, substance use, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). However, the reported GMV difference was identified using small-volume correction within a predefined DLPFC ROI and no whole-brain corrected between-group GMV result is reported; thus the study effectively reports only ROI findings. Inclusion criterion I3 (report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume) is not met. This violates exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between former heroin-dependent individuals and matched controls. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM two-sample t-test) with corrected results and provides peak MNI coordinates for clusters of reduced GM. Participant demographics, substance-use history (duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (DARTEL-based VBM) comparing smokers and age-matched non-smokers. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (smokers vs non-smokers) with AlphaSim-corrected voxelwise results and region coordinates/tables referenced, and also reports correlations with lifetime tobacco consumption (pack-years). Participant characteristics (all male, ages 23–40), substance-use measures (cigarettes/day, years, pack-years, light vs heavy groups), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. Thus it satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts), I4 (results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (key methodological/participant details provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter (GM) volume between heroin-dependent (opioid) subjects and matched healthy controls. It performs a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast and reports significant GM volume reductions (right PFC, left SMC, bilateral cingulate) with cluster-level statistics and references to table/figure results. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics (duration, dose, route, nicotine use), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2/SPM2, ANCOVA) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

E5 met: The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters (meets I5). However, all reported analyses focus on cerebellar lobular parcellation and regional volumetry (ROI-based analyses) rather than reporting any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast (no VBM or whole-brain SPM-style results), so it does not meet I3. Therefore it must be excluded under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorder vs controls that reports hippocampal (ROI) volumetry and overall tissue volumes, and it reports participant ages, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical tools (FMRIB FAST, AFNI). However, the paper does not present any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrasts — analyses and results are ROI-based (manual hippocampal tracings) and global tissue-volume comparisons only. Per the review criteria, studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results must be excluded (E5). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing treatment-naive alcohol-dependent individuals (n=24) to controls (n=17). It reports whole-brain measures (total cortical gray matter differences) and regional cortical gray matter volume differences (prefrontal and parietal regions) between groups, acquired on a 1.5T scanner with detailed preprocessing and statistical methods described. Participant demographics (male, ages described), substance use characteristics (lifetime duration, consumption), MRI field strength, and software/statistics (SAS PROC GLM) are reported. The study is not ROI-only (it includes whole-brain total cortical gray matter contrasts and regional analyses mapped in the Talairach system), so it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons and provides usable regional results relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing prescription opioid users to controls and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (meets I2 and I5). However, the VBM results presented derive from a priori/functional ROIs (L.NAc and L.vmPFC) extracted from rsFC findings rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and effectively reports ROI-only analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing chronic cigarette smokers (n=44) and matched non-smoker controls (n=44). The paper reports whole‑brain, voxel-wise two-sample t-test contrasts in SPM5/VBM5.1 with cluster-level reporting (thresholds and cluster sizes described) and identifies regions of reduced gray matter in smokers. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (cigarettes/day, years smoking), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study is not ROI-only and includes complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing chronic smokers (n=22) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts. The paper reports significant reductions in gray matter density in dlPFC and insula/operculum in smokers (with statistics), describes participant age/sex and smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies the review’s criteria for inclusion and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a longitudinal imaging study of first-episode schizophrenia patients treated with antipsychotics; it is not a study of substance users versus controls. It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing substance users to non-using controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports participant age/sex, some substance-use screening details, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results related to substance use). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (analyses are ROI-based/no qualifying whole-brain results relevant to substance-use contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for not addressing the review population/outcomes.

E5: Study reports only region-based volumetric analyses (Freesurfer segmentation of subcortical structures and global brain volumes) and regression/group comparisons, but does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (e.g., VBM or SPM voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing smokers vs controls on GM/brain volumes) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, smoking characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion not met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study that performed voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM volume differences (VBM results), including findings outside predefined ROIs (reported in Supporting Information Table S5), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Voxelwise results are provided (tables/figures) and methods report participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI VBM study but it compares two groups of smokers (quitters vs relapsers) rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I2 (requires GM differences between substance users and controls) nor I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). The paper does report participant sex/smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5 with DARTEL), satisfying I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E5 or E6) apply. Excluded on the basis that key inclusion criteria I2 and I3 are not met.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing heroin-dependent individuals (n=24) to matched controls (n=24). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (decreased GM volume in bilateral medial PFC, bilateral DLPFC, right fusiform) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR) and cluster thresholds; voxelwise results are described and supplementary material with tables/figures is indicated. Participant demographics (group sizes, sex), substance-use characteristics (heroin dependence, duration, methadone maintenance), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5, MATLAB) are provided. The study is neither ROI-only nor non-empirical. Core article sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI investigation of adolescent alcohol users versus non-users and reports gray-matter volume analyses (satisfies I2 and I5). However, the MRI analyses focus on preselected regions of interest (OFC and hippocampus) and report ROI-based volume comparisons rather than any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (I3) and provides no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results (I4 not met). As a result it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The provided “full text” is only an HTML skeleton without the article’s introduction, methods, results, or discussion. I cannot confirm this is an empirical structural MRI study comparing grey matter between methamphetamine users and controls or verify whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (cannot verify MRI GM comparisons), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts reported in the text provided), I4 (no voxelwise coordinates/figures available), I5 (participant and MRI/method details missing). No explicit exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are met from the available content, but full text is incomplete so review criteria cannot be applied. Excluding for inability to assess eligibility due to incomplete full text.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between heroin-dependent patients on methadone maintenance (n=27) and healthy controls (n=23). The paper reports whole-brain VBM between-group contrasts (SPM5/VBM5 with DARTEL), details MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software, and participant demographics and substance-use characteristics. Results list regional whole-brain GMV differences and report correlations; coordinate-based voxelwise results are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be included.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing alcoholic patients and controls and reports ROI-based gray matter volume analyses in predefined regions of interest (ventromedial PFC, superior frontal gyrus, supplementary motor area, etc.). However, the structural analyses are ROI-only (volumes extracted from ROIs) with no whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls) and I5 (participant demographics and scan details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM results). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only structural results with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The Methods and Results describe whole-brain VBM analyses (ANCOVA, DARTEL normalization, modulation) with reported widespread GM reductions in ADP versus HC (reported in main text and Supporting Information tables), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts. Participant demographics (age range, sex matching), substance-use measures (LDH, craving, days abstinent, relapse classification), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; empirical human structural MRI data). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that reports GM volume differences between substance users (heavy drinkers, including a smoking subgroup) and non-drinking controls. The paper provides whole-brain lobar and total neocortical GM comparisons (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, and total cortical GM) between groups, satisfying a whole-brain between-group contrast rather than only isolated ROIs. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/analysis methods are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or non-empirical status).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical gray matter volumes between chronic alcoholic men and healthy controls. The authors measured cortical gray matter (defined across the cortical mantle) and reported between-group contrasts and changes over time, satisfying whole-brain GM comparison requirements rather than an ROI-only approach. Participant demographic and substance-use information (age range, male sex, lifetime alcohol consumption) and MRI acquisition parameters (sequence details, TR/TE, FOV, matrix) are reported; although scanner field strength and voxelwise coordinate tables are not provided, the protocol and regional volumetric results meet the meta-analysis’ acceptable reporting standards and missing single items do not mandate exclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not a review). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommended for inclusion for analyses of alcohol-related GM differences.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant class) with healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts, cluster-level results and regional coordinates/figures, and describes participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSLVBM, CamBA). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; original human data). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

The provided full text (abstract and metadata) indicates regional/ROI volumetric analyses of cerebellar, pontine, thalamic, and cortical structures in alcoholics, but does not report or describe any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts. Therefore the study does not meet I3 (whole-brain evidence) and appears to report only ROI/regional results, triggering exclusion criterion E5. I2 (empirical MRI study of GM volume differences) appears satisfied based on reported regional volume comparisons between alcoholics and controls. Full text appears incomplete here (core methods/results not provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Exclusion: E5 (ROI-only, no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion met: I2. Inclusion not met: I3.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain VBM voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected) with cluster results presented in figures/tables, and describes participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI VBM study directly comparing smokers (nicotine users) and nonsmoking controls. The study used whole-brain coverage via a 1,024-ROI parcellation of the AAL atlas, performed VBM preprocessing (SPM8/VBM8) on 3T data, and applied multivariate classification to discriminate groups. Results include a map of consistent ROIs (N=150) and a table (Table 2) that lists ROIs with MNI center coordinates and sizes, satisfying the requirement that qualifying voxelwise/coordinate results be available. Participant demographics, smoking measures (FTND, CPD, lifetime usage), scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the primary analysis is a multivariate classifier rather than a conventional univariate voxelwise t-contrast, the paper provides whole-brain-derived regional results with coordinates and regression analyses relating GMV to smoking measures, which meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4; I5 (reporting details) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing older smokers (nicotine users) to matched never-smoker controls (N=39 pairs). The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts (SPM2) with cluster results and coordinates described, and authors reran thresholds to confirm robustness. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB, Stata) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No ROI-only or non-empirical study issues were identified. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This longitudinal MRI study reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness comparisons between adolescents who initiated alcohol use and non-users, identifying a significant cluster (right middle frontal gyrus) with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics, and also provides whole-brain analyses of other structural measures. Participant ages/sex, substance use characteristics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, FSL, SPM) are reported. Although the study uses cortical thickness (surface-based) rather than VBM gray-matter volume per se, it addresses structurally altered grey matter with whole-brain between-group contrasts and supplies coordinate results, satisfying the review objective to identify consistent regions of altered GM between substance users and controls.

This study compares two groups of alcohol users (recovering alcoholics vs actively heavily drinking subjects) and does not include a non-using healthy control group. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I2 (must assess GM differences between substance users and controls) nor I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). The provided content appears to be abstract/summary rather than the full article (fulltext_incomplete=true). No exclusion criteria (E5 or E6) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter between smokers (nicotine users: current/past) and nonsmokers. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM, SPM2) with regions surviving FWE correction, and provides participant age/sex, smoking definitions, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports manual volumetric (ROI) measurements of grey-matter structures (temporal lobe, superior temporal gyrus, hippocampus/amygdala) and DTI voxelwise analyses of FA/ADC (diffusion measures). While it is an empirical MRI study and reports participant demographics and scan parameters (meets I2 and I5), it does NOT report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of grey-matter volume (no VBM or whole-brain GM volume maps). The voxelwise analyses presented are of diffusion metrics (FA/ADC), not GM volume, and the volumetric results are ROI-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (no whole-brain GM contrast). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative/review-style summary of prior MRI studies of prenatal alcohol exposure rather than an original empirical structural MRI study reporting new human voxelwise whole-brain GM between-group contrasts or coordinate tables. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human structural MRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study reporting original GM volume differences between substance users and controls), I3 (no original whole-brain between-group GM contrast data presented), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of original results provided in this paper), I5 (as an overview it does not present a single study’s participant-level age/sex, MRI field strength, or preprocessing/statistical software as required for inclusion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods summary, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. However, it does not include any comparison between substance users and a control group (no between-group contrasts) and thus does not meet I2 (empirical MRI studies assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) nor I3 (reports whole-brain between-group contrasts).
